versions.short: The bill would direct the Secretary of the Interior, working with the Dakota Mainstem Regional Water System, Inc., to study whether the proposed Dakota Mainstem Water Supply Project, which would provide municipal, rural, and industrial water across parts of South Dakota, Iowa, Nebraska, and Minnesota, is technically and financially feasible. The Secretary would then prepare a report with recommendations on feasibility, whether the project should be authorized for construction, and a non-Federal share of construction costs of at least 25 percent, and would submit it to Congress and make it public. The bill would limit the federal share of study costs to 50 percent, cap federal study spending at $10,000,000, require the Secretary to identify funding sources within 90 days, and end the study authority five years after enactment.
